---
title: "Direction for fisheries simulation in SimSurvey 0.2.0"
output: html_document
---

This research note records the direction agreed for the next design milestone.
It does not describe an implemented API. First establish repository guidance,
formal tests, and focused fixes to the existing survey workflow.

## Population and catch

Start with one species and one fishery applied after `sim_distribution()`.
Attribute part of the existing total mortality to that fishery. For annual,
constant instantaneous mortality rates, Baranov catch in numbers is

\[
C_{f,a,y}=N_{a,y}\frac{F_{f,a,y}}{Z_{a,y}}(1-\exp(-Z_{a,y})).
\]

The fishery share and selectivity must jointly define fishing mortality before
calculating catch. Define the meaning of the share explicitly (for example,
age-specific F/Z versus the share at fully selected ages); do not silently apply
another selectivity curve to an already established catch budget. Handle zero
mortality without dividing by zero, and ensure allocated mortality never exceeds
total mortality. Call the unallocated remainder "other mortality," since it may
include other fisheries. See the [FAO population and catch model](https://www.fao.org/4/X9026E/x9026e06.htm).

Existing abundance trajectories already include Z. Do not subtract attributed
fishery deaths from subsequent abundance again. Existing annual spatial surfaces
do not propagate local depletion through movement or later years. A dynamic
fishing/effort feedback model would need a separate population design.

With fixed removals, relative effort and targeting allocate catches among cells
and operations. Increasing all effort cannot independently increase total catch;
the resulting CPUE is conditional on the catch budget. Bound spatial allocations
by available fish and the specified local mortality budget. Report infeasible
targets rather than silently clipping catches or reallocating outside accessible
areas. Decide the local mortality assumption before implementing allocation.

Keep retained catch, dead discards, live releases, and mortality distinct. Begin
with a simple all-retained scenario, leaving explicit extension points rather
than implying that observed legal landings equal all removals. Counts and lengths
do not define landed kilograms: add a weight relationship with explicit units.
Length-selective fishing must alter the joint age-length composition; drawing
unconditional lengths after selecting ages cannot represent arbitrary length
selectivity.

## Fishing activity

Separate knowledge (noise or lag in the perceived density signal) from targeting
strength (preference for high-signal cells). Include accessibility and exploration
in location choice. Distinguish the signal used to choose locations from the true
abundance available to catches, avoiding unintended extra density weighting.

Represent generic operations grouped into trips and landings, with stable
identifiers and explicit effort units. Gear-specific effort conversions can be
supplied without simulating vessel routing, economic optimization, or detailed
gear mechanics. Store aggregate catches and simulate only the individual fish
needed for biological samples rather than expanding every commercial catch.

## Monitoring as a separate observation process

The proposed separation is `sim_fishery()` for fishing truth and a subsequent
monitoring function for observations. Names beyond `sim_fishery()`, argument
contracts, and returned table schemas remain for the next design discussion.

Use independent controls for:

- Catch and effort reporting, including missing records and measurement error.
- Observer selection of trips and sampling of operations within selected trips.
- Port access, port/time strata, and selection of landings.
- Numbers of fish measured and random or length-stratified age samples.
- Tiered allocation among strata and selection within strata.

Preserve links among operations, trips, landings, and samples; retain inclusion
probabilities where the sampling design supplies them. Avoid using future true
catch to select an observer trip unless an explicitly idealized scenario requests
it. Preferential allocation among active ports can support valid weighted
inference when inclusion probabilities are known; convenience sampling and
zero-coverage groups present different limitations. More fish from the same
few trips do not replace more independent primary sampling units.

Program examples informing these abstractions:

- [Historical Northern cod protocols](https://waves-vagues.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/Library/40576838.pdf)
  describe distinct observer and port sampling strata, length samples, and
  length-stratified otolith collections (commercial catch-at-age questionnaire).
  These are historical protocols, not claims about current required coverage.
- [Alaska's 2026 deployment plan](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/s3/2026-01/Final_2026_ADP_akro.pdf)
  combines full coverage with randomized partial coverage and separates
  deployment strata and monitoring methods.
- [Ireland's 2021 sampling report](https://www.dcmap-ireland.ie/sites/default/files/DCF_Files/docs/Ireland_AR_2021_Text_20220531.pdf)
  illustrates prioritized port frames, landings-weighted selection, and subsequent
  sampling stages.

## CPUE and further design questions

Retain unsuccessful operations, separate missing catches from zeros, and preserve
effort units and catch definitions (retained or total). Define aggregate ratios
explicitly; a ratio of total catch to total effort differs from an unweighted
mean of operation-level ratios. Do not pool incompatible gear units. Initially
provide data suitable for downstream standardization rather than another fitted
index model. [Research on targeting and spatial effects](https://academic.oup.com/icesjms/article/83/9/fsag169/8788795)
illustrates why nominal CPUE need not track abundance proportionally.

Before implementation, settle share/selectivity semantics, the constrained
spatial allocation rule, effort units, retained/dead-discard defaults, the weight
relationship, and the minimal trip/landing sampling frames. Multiple fisheries
would require a shared mortality budget rather than independent unconstrained
calls. Seasonal surveys after fishing, persistent spatial depletion, learning,
age-reading error, and vessel efficiency trends are later extensions.
